title: Cap. IV Arg. 5 Sol cont: John 15:16 — we did not choose; do not confuse destined and temporal adoption
pass_a_gloss: Solution (continued). Augustine nearly runs through this first chapter to the Ephesians in explaining. I will add only these few things. The election which the Lord signified saying, You did not choose me, but I chose you; nor does faith itself precede. For not because we believed, but that we may believe he chose us, lest we be said to have chosen him first. By a dangerous error therefore they confuse destined adoption in the eternal act of the Divine election with perfect adoption in the temporal effect of efficacious vocation.
pass_b_english: Sol. (cont.) Augustine nearly walks this first chapter of Ephesians in explaining it. Only a few notes: the election the Lord meant by You did not choose me, but I chose you — and faith itself does not come first. He chose us not because we believed, but that we may believe, lest we be said to have chosen him first. So they dangerously confuse destined adoption in the eternal act of divine election with finished adoption in the temporal effect of efficacious vocation.
source_text: Sol. (cont.) Augustinus fere hoc caput primum ad Ephesios explicando percurrit. Apponam solummodo haec paucula. Electionem quam significavit Dominus dicens, Non vos me elegistis, sed ego vos elegi; nec fides ipsa praecedit. Non enim quia credidimus, sed ut credamus elegit nos, ne priores eum elegisse dicamur. Periculoso igitur errore confundunt destinatam adoptionem in aeterno actu electionis Divinae cum perfecta adoptione in temporali effectu vocationis efficacis.
